who: Adults in their 30s-40s who care about old friends but have no trigger to contact them
what_breaks: The intention to call a friend surfaces and evaporates within seconds because nothing external catches it at that moment.
quote: I really should call XY is such a common thought that fades away a second later. Even if it's someone I am really fond of.
volume_evidence: Comment in a 828-point HN thread with 487 comments ("A simple system I'm using to stay in touch with hundreds of people"), the top-voted keep-in-touch discussion on HN
workaround: Puts the person on his calendar or as a reminder, which he says is the only thing that actually makes him reach out

who: People who feel genuine affection for friends but have event-driven rather than interrupt-driven memory
what_breaks: They forget friends exist for months at a time and then hate themselves for it, which makes reaching out harder.
quote: i care deeply but seem to forget people exist and that makes me sad and dislike myself. i wish i could just remember. id still have so many friends if i did.
volume_evidence: Comment in the same 487-comment HN thread; the subthread it sits in drew 20+ replies arguing about whether forgetting friends means you don't care
workaround: None stated; explicitly says they wish they could just remember

who: Parents of young children with friends spread across time zones
what_breaks: Even when they do remember a friend, the remembering happens at an hour when calling is impossible, and the impulse dies there.
quote: There are a lot of people I care about, but sometimes you just _forget_. Or you remember, but it's too late to call them, or they're in a bad time zone
volume_evidence: Comment in the 487-comment HN keep-in-touch thread; several sibling comments describe the same post-kids collapse of friendships
workaround: Keeps friends' birthdays in a calendar to force at least one contact per year

who: People who maintain a hand-built spreadsheet of friends ranked by contact frequency
what_breaks: Staying in touch at adult scale only works if you keep a manual ranked database, because nothing in the phone tracks who has gone quiet.
quote: I've kept a spreadsheet for about 5 years of people I know from my hometown, from uni, past jobs, in other countries, family of friends, etc... ranked roughly by how frequently to contact them
volume_evidence: One of at least eight separate commenters in the same 487-comment thread who independently describe building a spreadsheet, Airtable base, Notion doc or text file of friends
workaround: Five-year-old personal spreadsheet of people ranked by desired contact frequency

who: People who left Facebook and lost the birthday and life-event feed that used to prompt them
what_breaks: Without a social feed there is no ambient signal that a friend has gone months without contact, so they scroll their SMS history by hand to find who dropped off.
quote: The last step is going through my text message history, which is conveniently ordered by last contact. I skip down about two months, and then work my way down the list
volume_evidence: Comment by a well-known HN user in the 487-comment thread; sits alongside many other self-described manual systems
workaround: Recurring calendar items for each friend's birthday, plus a manual scroll down the text-message list every couple of months and a full contact review each Christmas

who: People who refuse to pay for a personal CRM and instead hand-maintain a relationship list in Apple Reminders
what_breaks: Setting up and maintaining the list of who to contact and when is entirely manual, and there is nothing that automates keeping it current.
quote: I do literally have a Reminders list called "Maintain relationships" with actions like "Buy a birthday card for my niece", "Call Mom on her wedding anniversary", "Text Joe"
volume_evidence: Comment in the Show HN thread for Nat.app (53 points, 39 comments); the author says he would pay a couple of dollars a month just to automate maintaining this list
workaround: A manually built Apple Reminders list named "Maintain relationships" with one recurring item per person

who: People who find out secondhand that something major happened to a friend they let drift
what_breaks: The cost of the lapse only becomes visible at the worst moment, when they hear about a crisis or a milestone years after losing contact.
quote: I feel really, really guilty if I hear something great or awful happened to someone I used to be in touch with, but the relationship faded away into the flow of life.
volume_evidence: Comment in a 414-point HN thread with 198 comments about the Monica personal CRM
workaround: Started using Monica, a self-hosted personal CRM

who: Immigrants and third-culture adults whose family lives overseas
what_breaks: Thinking about family abroad does not convert into contact; the thought and the action are disconnected, and repeated failed attempts taught them not to try.
quote: I think about people all the time, but it doesn't trigger my reaching out.
volume_evidence: Comment in the 487-comment HN keep-in-touch thread; the poster describes growing up moving countries with all family overseas
workaround: None; describes it as learned helplessness and waits for annual in-person visits

who: Adult children who forget to call a parent despite wanting to
what_breaks: A recurring calendar event for "call Mom" fires on days they already called, so the reminder becomes noise and gets ignored.
quote: Calendar events didn't work, because sometimes I did contact her that day, and was notified to call her anyway.
volume_evidence: Show HN post for "Call Your Mother"; the author built an app specifically because calendar reminders failed this way, and the pattern recurs across later personal-CRM threads
workaround: Built his own app that tracks last contact instead of firing on a fixed schedule

who: People who tried a dedicated personal CRM and abandoned it within months
what_breaks: The app requires manual upkeep that nobody sustains, so the data goes stale and the tool silently stops working.
quote: the friction of yet another specialized tool kept me from actively maintaining it, which of course makes it entirely worthless.
volume_evidence: Comment in the 414-point/198-comment Monica HN thread; at least three commenters in that thread describe trying and abandoning it for the same reason
workaround: Fell back to Google Contacts with birthday reminders and custom fields

who: People who meant to follow up with someone they just met and never did
what_breaks: They intend to text someone when they are near them or fresh off a meeting, but the intention only surfaces after the moment has passed.
quote: I end up doing this manually and I always forget folks until it's too late.
volume_evidence: Comment in the Launch HN thread for Dex (189 points, 141 comments)
workaround: Manually texts people when he happens to notice he is in their part of town

who: Long-running Duolingo users with 800+ day streaks
what_breaks: Preserving the streak displaces the goal entirely: they perform a fake token session at 1am rather than lose the counter.
quote: I had a 800+ day streak and I remember that on the days I couldn't practice, I used to play Duolingo story #1 at 1am with half eyes open just to keep it going.
volume_evidence: Comment in a 255-point HN thread with 225 comments titled "It's quite hard to lose a Duolingo streak"; a dozen commenters in the same thread describe gaming or mourning their streak
workaround: Repeating the easiest possible lesson late at night purely to preserve the number

who: Language learners who abandoned study the day the streak broke
what_breaks: One missed midnight cutoff ends not just the streak but the entire habit, permanently.
quote: I was learning several languages and one day at 12:01am I lost a streak. That crushed me. From then on I haven't touched Dulolingo.
volume_evidence: Comment in the 255-point/225-comment HN Duolingo streak thread; at least four other commenters in the same thread report quitting outright after losing a streak
workaround: None; quit the app entirely

who: Habit-app users whose life circumstances changed (new baby, illness, travel)
what_breaks: The tracker has no concept of a legitimate reason to miss a day, so a real-life event terminates a 1000-day practice.
quote: In fact I lost my 1000+ day streak 2 months ago (a newborn will do that to you) and haven't done a single Duolingo lesson since then.
volume_evidence: Comment in the 255-point/225-comment HN Duolingo streak thread
workaround: Switched to a spaced-repetition flashcard app with no streak

who: People who anticipate the streak break and dread it before it happens
what_breaks: The streak becomes a liability they want to disable, because they know the eventual break will demotivate them more than the streak ever motivated them.
quote: I knew it was just a matter of time before I had my streak broken, and I was very concerned about what would happen then.
volume_evidence: Comment in the 255-point/225-comment HN Duolingo streak thread; the commenter notes there is no way to turn streaks off
workaround: Wanted to turn streaks off; the product does not allow it

who: Daily-practice app users whose reminder arrives after the window when they could act
what_breaks: The reminder fires too late in the day to actually do the lesson, which is what causes the miss.
quote: I'm rather pissed if the daily reminder comes to late.
volume_evidence: Comment in the 255-point/225-comment HN Duolingo streak thread
workaround: Says if it keeps failing he will turn off notifications or uninstall

who: Beeminder users with money on the line who quietly falsify their own logs
what_breaks: They log the task as done just before the midnight deadline and do it hours later, or not at all, turning the accountability system into theater.
quote: saying at 11:56pm that I'd meditated for 5 minutes, but not actually doing the meditation until I went to bed at 2am.
volume_evidence: Beeminder forum thread "New Years Resolution: no weaseling" (1,124 views, 22 likes); the community has a standing vocabulary for this ("weaseling") and dozens of threads about weasel-proofing
workaround: Publicly declared a no-weaseling resolution on the forum for accountability

who: People who pay money to a commitment device and then edit their past data to avoid the penalty
what_breaks: When they are emotionally overwhelmed, the part of them that set the goal loses to the part that can edit the record.
quote: I have an issue with getting into challenging emotional spaces where my inner weasel takes over and edits previous entries to prevent derail.
volume_evidence: Beeminder forum thread with 663 views; part of a larger cluster of "cheat-proof" and "weasel-proof" request threads spanning 2015-2024
workaround: Asked to hand account credentials to a coach or friend so he physically cannot edit his own history

who: People who know an app cannot hold them accountable the way a person can
what_breaks: A reminder or a bot can be dismissed with zero social cost, so self-reporting systems fail exactly where a human check-in would not.
quote: You can dismiss the reminder or ignore it. For a lot of people, lying to another person and saying "I'm working" when actually you're not is a pretty difficult thing to do.
volume_evidence: Comment by the founder of a human accountability service on HN, in the Show HN thread for "Make Me Work"
workaround: Paid human check-ins instead of automated reminders

who: Goal-tracker users who are technically "on track" and therefore stop doing the thing
what_breaks: Once they have buffer, the nagging stops, and without the nag they simply don't do the habit that day.
quote: once in the safety buffer I forget to do the things – simply because I don't have a nagging "+1 due on $goal until 00:00"
volume_evidence: Beeminder forum feature request with 398 views; the same poster has a separate 18-post, 684-view thread arguing reminders are the product's weak point
workaround: Asked for an opt-in daily nudge; notes that the existing "lead days" setting just clutters notifications until he ignores all of them

who: Long-term commitment-device users who cycle through months of engagement and months of collapse
what_breaks: Engagement comes in seasons; they archive their goals when the system stops landing, and the notifications are what fail first.
quote: I will say that I think notifications might be the fail point. They just get missed or don't happen or whatever - same difference to the human I suppose.
volume_evidence: Beeminder forum thread "Beeminder Seasons" (220 views); multiple long-time users in the thread report the same cycle
workaround: Archives goals for months at a time, then restarts; has considered hiring a human "nannybot"

who: People whose reminders keep firing after the task is already done
what_breaks: The reminder has no idea whether the thing happened, so it shows up anyway and trains the person to ignore every future one.
quote: Except then these reminders would still show up when I'm sone with the thing for that day. Which means I will eventually start to ignore them.
volume_evidence: Beeminder forum thread "More Reminder Settings please" (18 posts, 684 views, 28 likes); staff reply acknowledges conflicting demands and no fix
workaround: Tried Google Calendar reminders on the home screen and rejected them for the same reason

who: People who get reminded in the wrong room at the wrong hour
what_breaks: The reminder reaches them where they cannot act on it, so it is functionally the same as no reminder.
quote: what I'm hoping for is a technological solution that reminds me in the right place and time (upstairs, right before I go to bed) instead of the wrong place (downstairs on the computer).
volume_evidence: Beeminder forum thread (8 posts, 966 views); the poster says he "keeps invalidly derailing" because of it, and two other users plus staff say they are trying to solve the same problem with Raspberry Pi lights and IFTTT
workaround: Tried to wire a smart plug and nightlight through IFTTT so a physical light upstairs would signal unfinished tasks before bed

who: People who have gone notification-blind to their own goal app
what_breaks: A normal push notification is dismissed reflexively, so only an alarm that must be manually killed still registers.
quote: Without needing to manually dismiss them I would always end up ignoring the Beeminder notifications after a while.
volume_evidence: Beeminder forum post (151 views); a separate thread makes the same complaint about notification sound, and a 2024 thread names notifications as the product's fail point
workaround: Installed a third-party Android app (AlertMe) to convert goal notifications into alarm-style alerts he must dismiss by hand

who: People whose important reminders are indistinguishable from every other app's push
what_breaks: The alert that matters sounds exactly like the alerts that don't, so it gets swiped away with the rest.
quote: I rely on the iOS app to remind me about beemergencies, but too often I end up ignoring the notification because it sounds like my other notifications.
volume_evidence: Beeminder forum feature request; part of a recurring pattern across at least four separate reminder threads in the same forum
workaround: Requested custom notification sounds, as another to-do app offers

who: People who capture tasks by voice or note and never act on them
what_breaks: Recording the intention feels like handling it, so the note becomes a substitute for doing the thing rather than a trigger to do it.
quote: It could easily become a tool which gives a false sense of handling a task when really it just blackholes the thought into an ever growing collection of 3-second notes that are never revisited.
volume_evidence: Comment in a 593-point HN thread with 588 comments about the Pebble Index voice-capture ring; multiple replies in the subthread debate exactly this failure mode
workaround: Others in the thread describe manual triage routines to stop notes from black-holing

who: Commuters who think of a home task while driving and have no way to bind it to arriving home
what_breaks: The assistant nominally supports "remind me when I get home" but fails in practice, so the thought has to be re-remembered at the door.
quote: You'd expect Siri or Google Assistant to be able to do this and in theory they can but in practice they suck for this use case.
volume_evidence: Comment in the 593-point/588-comment HN Pebble Index thread; a March 2025 HN thread on Siri (88 points, 79 comments) has a highly-upvoted comment reporting the exact same command failing
workaround: Android quick-settings button that opens a blank email to himself; he triages the inbox later

who: iPhone users who try to set location-based reminders by voice
what_breaks: The single most useful reminder form (fire when I arrive somewhere) fails on a detail the phone already knows.
quote: "Siri, remind me when I get home to <task>." -> "Sorry, I don't have your address."
volume_evidence: Comment in an 88-point HN thread with 79 comments ("Leaked Apple meeting shows how dire the Siri situation is"); commenter lists four such failures from a two-week period
workaround: Says it has become a game in his household whether Siri will complete a request at all

who: People who built a personal pipeline to get captured thoughts in front of themselves again
what_breaks: No assistant closes the loop between capturing a thought and resurfacing it when action is possible, so they wire it themselves.
quote: My current setup involves an Apple shortcut that sends a text blob to my email inbox with the subject "Note to self"
volume_evidence: Comment in the 593-point/588-comment HN Pebble Index thread; at least two other commenters describe near-identical email-to-self capture pipelines
workaround: Apple Shortcut to self-email with a fixed subject line, a mail filter into a dedicated folder, and manual triage into an action planner

who: People who need the nudge at the one moment they can still act, not before or after
what_breaks: An alert is only useful if it lands in the narrow window where doing the thing is still possible; outside that window it is noise.
quote: that threat is only effective if you remember that there is a threat and are aware that you are in danger of going off track at the specific time you can do something about it
volume_evidence: Beeminder forum thread "More Reminder Settings please" (18 posts, 684 views, 28 likes)
workaround: Requesting per-goal reminder time windows the product does not offer
